source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's OCB1 campus in Council Bluffs publishes 9 MW of IT capacity across 420,000 square feet, the largest published power figure of Iowa's two documented facilities.

The published number is a ceiling on what the campus can deliver, not a description of what runs inside it. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 9 MW supports roughly 225 racks. At 10 kW per rack it supports roughly 900. CyrusOne publishes no rack count, no accelerator count, and no tenant list, so neither figure describes installed hardware. The certifications, PCI DSS, HIPAA, FISMA, TIA-942, and HITRUST, qualify the facility for regulated workloads. They do not establish that any particular tenant or training cluster is present.

Iowa holds 52 mapped facilities, and only two publish a megawatt figure, totaling 18 MW. OCB1 is half that published total and ranks first in the state by published capacity. The gap between 52 mapped sites and two published figures is the signal that matters for AI scaling: most Iowa capacity is invisible in the public record. Published megawatts describe a small, documented slice of a much larger buildout, and the binding constraint on where compute lands is often the power and buildings that never appear in an operator spec page at all.

What this data does not cover is equally important. It carries no announced expansion, no interconnection queue position, no utility, no power purchase agreement, and no construction timeline. It cannot say whether OCB1's 9 MW is fully energized, partially leased, or reserved for a tenant that has not been named. It also cannot say how the other 50 Iowa facilities are powered or how large they are. The 18 MW state total is a floor set by disclosure practice, not a measurement of Iowa data center load.
